findings.title: CandidateV2 has nowhere to record native signing, architecture and extracted-archive audit results, and gates A-C are never derived
findings.claim: Mac-1a Task 4 asks auditCandidate to run codesign on the original and extracted bundle, ad-hoc display checks on helpers, lipo/file ARM64 checks on every Mach-O file, a separate spctl assessment and a bundle inventory comparison. The CandidateV2 it returns has no fields for any of these results: signing is only the label 'windows-private'|'adhoc', and there is no inventory digest. Task 6 hands off the candidate 'with required native checks attached' but defines no schema for the attachment. Mac-1b Task 5 says how gates D, E and F are derived but never says where the A, B and C inputs come from or how they are validated.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L62-72 (CandidateV2 fields), L119 (native checks), L139 ('required native checks attached'); 1b plan L109 (buildComplete=A, macRuntimeVerified=A+B+C), L114 (only D/E/F derivations); spec L153 and L157 (required observations, recorded separately), spec L61 ('signing state').
findings.why: A manifest can claim 'adhoc' with no proof attached. Mac-1b's readiness aggregate then gates every outcome on A-C without a validated evidence contract, so buildComplete or macRuntimeVerified could be set from free-text README rows. That is false evidence.
findings.fix: Add a strict `nativeAudit` object to CandidateV2, with a darwin variant: codesignVerify {original, extracted}, adhocBundles [{path, ok}], machO [{path, arch}], spctl {outcome}, and inventorySha256 plus an extractedInventoryMatch flag. Give win32 its own variant. Have parseCandidateV2 reject a darwin candidate with a missing or failed audit. Define Gate A/B/C evidence schemas in Mac-1b Task 5 (test logs or summaries by hash, the native smoke reports, the Mac-1a manual checklist) and test their derivation.

findings.title: The Windows half of a paired v2 report has no defined independent cleanup proof
findings.claim: Mac-1b requires every CrossPlatformRunV2, including the Windows side, to carry independent cleanup proof from the Mac-1a owner. Mac-1a Task 5 defines CleanupProof through ProcessIdentity {pid, ppid, pgid, start} and ps sampling only. Windows has no pgid, and the plan says Windows 'retains taskkill /PID /T behavior' with no before/after inventory source.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L128 (ProcessIdentity requires pgid; Windows keeps taskkill); 1b plan L47 ('independent cleanup proof'), L64 ('Use Mac-1a process-tree owner'); scripts/network/lease-smoke-lifecycle.ts:L29-32 (Windows taskkill, POSIX SIGKILL of the root only).
findings.why: When the Windows driver runs, the implementer must either invent a proof (false evidence) or the pair validator rejects every Windows report, which blocks gates D and E.
findings.fix: Specify a Windows adapter in Task 5. For example, sample with a bounded PowerShell `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` query giving ProcessId, ParentProcessId and CreationDate, called through an execFile argument array. Make pgid optional or platform-discriminated, with start = CreationDate, and make CleanupProof a platform-discriminated union. Add fake-table tests for Windows, and have Mac-1b Task 1 validate the per-platform variant.

findings.title: Failing on input overflow with a 512 cap will fail ordinary captures, because every outgoing held frame is recorded
findings.claim: Mac-1b Task 2 keeps the 512-input cap and says to 'count and fail any overflow of ... input records'. The existing observer records every outgoing input-class packet, including the unreliable held frames the client sends on each send() call. Today it only avoids failing by silently shifting the ring. The plan does not say which inputs must be retained. The schema only needs command inputs to match applied results.
findings.evidence: 1b plan L20, L63; scripts/network/online-app-observer.ts:L40-46 (every outgoing input pushed; shift when over 512); src/renderer/src/clientControl/clientRun.ts:L190 (a held frame per send); scripts/network/internet-app-report.ts:L18, L43 (inputs max 512; results must match an input that has a command).
findings.why: A 30-540 s capture of two players moving can easily send more than 512 held frames. The v2 driver would then fail ordinary sessions, or the implementer would quietly bring truncation back.
findings.fix: Define retention explicitly. Retain every command input and the first held input (order evidence) up to the cap, and count all other held frames in totals without retaining them. Fail only if retained command or required boundary records overflow. Test a long held stream that passes and more than 512 commands that fail.

findings.title: No source is defined for the modeId in logical identity
findings.claim: readLogicalIdentity requires a modeId, and pairing compares it. auditCandidate's options and the CLI flags in Task 4 include no mode, and the plan never says which registered mode the packaged online app uses or how that is checked against the compiled output.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L48, L81 (readLogicalIdentity(root, revision, modeId, serviceOrigin)), L116 (auditCandidate options lack modeId; CLI adds platform/revision/service-origin/deployment only); src/network/modes/sector.ts:L19 (modeId 'sector'); src/network/modes/registry.ts:L11.
findings.why: Without a defined source, each side may hard-code or pass its own value, so a mode-identity check means nothing, or the two sides disagree.
findings.fix: Add `modeId` to the auditCandidate options and an explicit `--mode-id` flag, validated against the registered mode definitions (sector today). Alternatively, derive it from the online mode registry in source and state that. Test an unknown mode being rejected.

findings.title: The new formatVersions.ts is not added to the explicit content-digest file list
findings.claim: Task 1 creates src/shared/formatVersions.ts and moves the checkpoint and replay format values into it, imported by the authority code. computeContentDigest hashes a fixed list of src/shared files plus walked directories, and src/shared/formatVersions.ts is not in that list. The plan says 'exclude no game source from digest' but never tells the implementer to add the file.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L79-85; build/contentDigest.ts:L12-16 (fixed src/shared list); src/renderer/src/authority/checkpoint.ts:L34, L49 (literal 2 that moves to the constant).
findings.why: After the change, editing the checkpoint or replay format constant no longer changes the runtime compatibility digest that peers compare. Only the evidence-level fields would still catch it, which weakens gameplay compatibility.
findings.fix: In Task 1, add 'src/shared/formatVersions.ts' to the computeContentDigest paths. Add a test that changing the file changes the digest. Note the digest change in the commit.

findings.title: The rejected-prepareExit test contradicts current onlineExit, and onlineExit.ts is not in Task 3's file list
findings.claim: Task 3 says to race close, quit and a rejected prepareExit and 'assert one prepareExit/dispose chain'. In registerOnlineExit, dispose is chained with .then after prepareExit, so a rejection skips dispose from that path. owner.dispose itself also chains on prepareExit, so it would reject too. Task 3 modifies only index.ts and appMenu.ts, and says registerOnlineExit stays the only exit owner.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L103, L105, L107; src/main/network/onlineExit.ts:L12-15; src/main/network/onlineSession.ts:L531-537, L553.
findings.why: The planned test either fails against code the task may not change, or gets weakened. Either way the failed-save retirement path (Review Focus 3) is left unproven.
findings.fix: State the expected behavior: dispose runs (or helpers are force-retired) even after prepareExit rejects. Either add onlineExit.ts to Task 3 with a `.finally`/catch-then-dispose change and a test, or change the assertion to the existing guarantee (quit still happens; helper retirement comes from the IPC remove path). Then rely on Task 6 native evidence.

findings.title: Detached POSIX groups no longer receive the terminal's Ctrl+C or SIGHUP; the controller has no signal-cleanup contract
findings.claim: Task 5 requires POSIX children to be spawned detached in their own process groups. Detached groups are outside the terminal's foreground group, so an operator's Ctrl+C or a closed terminal kills only the controller and leaves Electron trees orphaned. The Mac-1b Task 4 runner is operator-driven through stdin, which makes interrupting it likely.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L128, L131; 1b plan L95, L99; scripts/network/internet-app-smoke.ts:L36 (current non-detached spawn).
findings.why: This is a new leak path created by the ownership change, on the very machines where the test sessions run, and the stated cleanup guarantee does not cover it.
findings.fix: Have owned-process.ts install SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP handlers, plus a stdin-close handler, in the controller. These run stop() on every registered tree within the deadline, write the failure report, then exit. Add fake tests and a native probe case that interrupts the controller.

findings.title: Committed evidence references unsanitized candidate manifests by hash
findings.claim: CandidateV2 carries packagePath and os/tools, and Mac-1a allows local absolute paths in private candidate files. Both plans commit evidence. The Mac-1b readiness CLI verifies the hash of every referenced file, including candidate manifests, so a sanitized copy no longer matches, and committing the original leaks the user's absolute home path.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L66, L75, L137, L145; 1b plan L47 (run carries the candidate manifest reference/hash), L107 (CLI verifies every referenced file hash); spec L90 (no private user data in the package).
findings.why: Either the evidence chain breaks or private paths end up in git.
findings.fix: Store packagePath as a path relative to the evidence or output root, or as a sanitized label, and keep absolute paths only in an uncommitted sidecar. Have parseCandidateV2 reject absolute or home-directory paths in committed variants. Test that a manifest containing /Users/ or C:\Users\ is rejected.

findings.title: Several recovery scenarios have no driver mechanism
findings.claim: The stdin command set (baseline, capture, restart-guest, kill-host, stale-probe, finish) has nothing that causes or marks guest-disconnect, quit or close. stale-probe replays 'a previously recorded old-generation control message' without saying which link, message class or recording point, even though fencing tears down the old link. It also leaves unclear whether the recorded bytes could include a ticket or seat token.
findings.evidence: 1b plan L71 (scenario list), L95 (commands), L99 (never persist raw secrets); src/shared/roomSession.ts:L23, L58 (auth frames carry ticket and connectionId).
findings.why: An implementer has to invent the choreography for three gate-F scenarios. The stale probe could be built as an injection outside ordinary paths, or could keep a token-bearing frame.
findings.fix: Add an operator-marked `disconnect` (network drop, then rejoin) and `quit`/`close` markers, or a documented human action plus recorder event, for those scenarios. Specify that stale-probe re-sends only a recorded RTC data-channel input or state packet (never service auth frames) from the old-generation binding to the current host, and that the recorder rejects keys matching the existing sensitive-key regex.

findings.title: The Mac-1a candidate handoff conflicts with Mac-1b's rebuild and exact-source verification
findings.claim: Mac-1a Task 6 says to hand off its CandidateV2 and archive to Mac-1b. sourceFiles covers scripts/**, and Mac-1b modifies scripts, so the Mac-1a candidate cannot pass the ancestor plus exact-source check under the Mac-1b driver. Mac-1b Task 6 correctly freezes and rebuilds.
findings.evidence: 1a plan L139; 1b plan L121; scripts/network/candidate-manifest.ts:L24 (sourceFiles includes scripts); scripts/network/internet-app-smoke.ts:L91.
findings.why: This may mislead an executor into reusing a stale candidate.
findings.fix: Reword 1a L139: the Mac-1a candidate is Mac-1a evidence only, and Mac-1b Task 6 builds new candidates after its tooling merges.
